newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ reconfirms June MPS position remains intact.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ reconfirms June MPS position remains intact.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand, in answer to questions from Reuters on Tuesday, confirmed its positions on monetary policy expressed in its June statement remained unchanged.

A spokesman said that the bank's desired conditions had not changed, that the 2:1 ratio relating the currency and bank bills had not changed and that comments relating to the bank's comfort zone on the Monetary Conditions Index still applied.
Asked to comment if conditions were too easy, the spokesman said the bank declined.
The bank said it wanted the MCI -- a composite of the New Zealand dollar's Trade-Weighted Index and the 90-day bank bill rate -- to average 825 over the September quarter.
Shortly before Tuesday morning's jobs data the index had fallen to 723, some 102 basis points easier than the desired level.

In June, bank Governor Don Brash said that as a very approximate guideline, he would expect actual monetary conditions to be within a range or plus or minus 50 MCI points from the desired level in the weeks immediately following a comprehensive inflation projection.
He said that as more data came to hand over the quarter and as the last comprehensive inflation projection receded into history, "we may be rather more tolerant".
Brash said then that the comfort zone was not a binding rule which the bank could be expected to follow in all circumstances.
"Those expecting us to do so are likely to be disappointed."
The MCI tightened to 750 at 11.45 a.m. (2345 GMT).

The market had expected the jobs data to be weaker than the RB had forecast but it was in fact stronger, particularly the critical hours worked figures which the bank watches closely because it is a leading, rather than lagging, indicator.
